topic_title: Top 7 Best Dog Breeds That Get Along With Cats
intro: Finding a dog that can peacefully coexist with your feline friends is all about choosing breeds known for their gentle nature and lower prey drives. While every dog is an individual, some breeds tend to be calmer around small animals and less likely to chase or stress out cats. Whether you want a playful companion or a laid-back buddy, these breeds have earned their reputation for being more cat-friendly. Here’s a carefully selected list of dog breeds that often thrive in homes with cats, ranked from good fits to the very best companions for your kitty.

picks.description: Golden Retrievers are famously friendly and adaptable dogs who often do well with cats. Their easygoing temperament and social nature mean they’re typically not aggressive or overly curious in a way that disturbs small animals. They enjoy company and tend to accept cats as part of the family when properly introduced. While they are energetic and love to play, their generally patient attitude helps smooth interactions with feline housemates. Because they’re so people-focused, they often see cats as just another member of the household to befriend rather than chase.
picks.best_for: Families seeking a friendly, social dog that can coexist with cats
picks.quirky_fact: Golden Retrievers love to 'soft mouth' carry things gently, which can make them extra careful around smaller pets.

picks.description: Standard Poodles are intelligent, trainable, and known for their calm demeanor, making them a great fit in homes with cats. They tend to have lower prey drives compared to some other breeds, which means they’re less likely to chase or stress out small animals. Their keen intelligence means they learn quickly how to behave around cats, especially with consistent training. Plus, their low-shedding coat is a bonus for mixed-species households. Standard Poodles are affectionate and often enjoy the companionship of other pets, forming close bonds with feline friends when introduced thoughtfully.
picks.best_for: Homes wanting a smart, calm companion alongside cats
picks.quirky_fact: Poodles were originally bred as water retrievers, but their elegant poofs make them look like little aristocrats.

picks.description: Cavaliers are sweet-natured, gentle dogs that usually get along famously with cats. Their mellow and affectionate personalities make them less likely to exhibit aggressive or overly energetic behavior around smaller animals. They’re known for being extremely people- and pet-friendly, often seeking out companionship wherever they find it. Their moderate activity level means they can enjoy playtime without overwhelming a cat. Cavaliers tend to be quite adaptable, so they can adjust well to living with feline friends, especially with patient introductions and supervision at first.
picks.best_for: Loving households looking for a gentle dog to share life with cats
picks.quirky_fact: This breed’s expressive eyes earned them the nickname 'the little lion dog' in their royal English history.

picks.description: Havanese dogs are lively yet gentle and often form strong bonds with cats in the home. They tend to be curious but not aggressive, showing a playful interest rather than predatory behavior toward small animals. Their social and affectionate nature means they enjoy the company of other pets and people alike. Havanese are also small enough not to intimidate cats, which can help ease tension during introductions. With consistent positive socialization, they usually learn to coexist peacefully and even enjoy the company of their feline roommates.
picks.best_for: Families wanting a small, friendly dog that thrives with cats
picks.quirky_fact: Havanese are known as 'the Velcro dog' because they love to stick close to their favorite people and pets.

picks.description: Bichon Frises are cheerful, playful, and tend to be quite gentle around cats. Their affectionate personalities and moderate energy levels mean they’re unlikely to overwhelm a feline friend. Bichons enjoy social settings and often get along well with other animals if introduced properly. They’re smart and responsive, making it easier to train them to respect boundaries with cats. Plus, their low-shedding coats can be a bonus for multi-pet households concerned about dander or hair. Overall, Bichons are a friendly breed that can add a joyful presence to a home with cats.
picks.best_for: Pet owners looking for a lively yet gentle companion alongside cats
picks.quirky_fact: Bichon Frises often have a happy, smiling expression that’s hard to resist.

picks.description: Great Danes are gentle giants known for their calm and laid-back nature, which often makes them surprisingly good companions for cats. Despite their large size, they’re typically very patient and tolerant, showing a relaxed attitude that can help keep the peace with feline housemates. Their low prey drive and affectionate demeanor mean they usually won’t chase or harass smaller animals. While their size means supervision is wise during introductions, Great Danes often enjoy the company of cats and can form close bonds that are both heartwarming and enduring.
picks.best_for: Homes with space looking for a calm, cat-friendly gentle giant
picks.quirky_fact: Great Danes are so tall they can often see over fences without jumping!

picks.description: English Springer Spaniels are widely recognized for their balanced temperament and lower prey drive, making them excellent companions for cats. They’re energetic but also remarkably gentle and social dogs who usually adapt well to multi-pet households. Their friendly nature and eagerness to please mean they take well to training that encourages calm, respectful behavior around cats. Springers are affectionate and thrive on companionship, often forming tight bonds with feline housemates. With proper introduction and positive reinforcement, they’re one of the best breed choices for peaceful dog-cat cohabitation.
picks.best_for: Active families wanting a friendly dog that respects cats
picks.quirky_fact: English Springer Spaniels are natural water lovers, often happily splashing around in ponds or lakes.
